descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P1 · our extension of a stated behaviour · ours: odd input (email letter case).

Approach · OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · S25 An email in a different case signs in to the same physician, not a second one (at the sign-in route)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U6 Open sign-up: a new email that was never invited signs in with the emailed code. The physician is created and appears in the physician list. (UAT OAT-01 step 6; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 13) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given The local stack's auth API and an unseeded address qa-case-<tag>@roundai.test

When Issue a code for the lower-case address and POST /api/auth/sign-in/email-otp with QA-Case-<tag>@RoundAI.test and that code; record the acceptance; sign out; sign in again with the lower-case address.

Then There is one Better Auth user row for the address. The second sign-in reuses it: the acceptance is found and the agreements screen is not due again.

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): U6 / AC 13 'end up in the same physician list': two user rows for one address, or an acceptance not found on the second sign-in, = Fail. The UI cannot show this, because AuthGate lower-cases the email before sending (src/components/auth/AuthGate.tsx), so the earlier browser version of this case could never fail. Which table counts as the physician list is Q4. …

Where it ran: local newspec-a (new Playwright specs); test method API · API (Convex functions); lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S25 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/OAT-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-a.

Test method: API · API (Convex functions); secondary: CODEREVIEW · Code review — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on local; Source: newspec-a.

UAT item: OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · Section: B · Operational Acceptance Tests · Scenario: OAT-01/S25

An email in a different case signs in to the same physician, not a second one (at the sign-in route)

Tickets: TFA-94513 Signing In & Session Security (in progress)

New local lane newspec-a: status passed in newspec-a/results.json → passed (passed).

How it is tested (newspec-a/plan.json, automatable: yes): New api spec: fresh unseeded address qa-case-<tag>@roundai.test; issue a code for the lower-case form (seed:issueTestOtp) and POST /api/auth/sign-in/email-otp with QA-Case-<tag>@RoundAI.test; record the acceptance; sign out; sign in again lower-case; compare user ids and agreements:current acceptedVersion; count user rows with that email (betterAuth user table via the convex CLI, filtered by the test's address before parsing, rows split by raw newlines joined back). — Pure auth-route calls on the local stack.

Detail:

QA-Case-<tag>@RoundAI.test signs in (200) with a code issued for the lower-case form; the stored email is lower-case; after sign-out the lower-case address signs in to the SAME user id; the acceptance made on the first sign-in is found (acceptedVersion = version 2026-10-05, screen not due); exactly one Better Auth user row for the address (read with the convex CLI from the betterAuth component). Re-run in final2 after making the user-row read robust (filtered by the test's own address; rows split by another job's raw newline are joined back): still exactly one row, same user id.

Evidence: 2 attached.
